title: Roman Numeral Converter
story: Roman numerals dominated the ancient world and still appear on clock faces, movie credits, and Super Bowls. Converting 2024 to MMXXIV isn't magic — it's a systematic algorithm. Build the converter and read any Roman numeral.
why: Roman numeral conversion teaches value-to-symbol mapping with arrays, descending-order greedy algorithms, and string building — all in one practical program.
analogy: Making change with coins: to give $47, you start with the largest bill ($20), give two (now $40 left), then a $5 ($45 left), then two $1s. Roman numerals are 'making change' with symbol-values: start big, work down to I. Greedy and optimal.
try_it: Write the reverse: `from_roman(s: Str) -> Int` that parses a Roman numeral back to a number. Handle invalid numerals. Add a `requires` that input is 1-3999 (standard Roman range). Convert your birth year to Roman numerals.
tips: The 13 symbol-value pairs include subtractive forms (IV=4, IX=9, etc.)
Greedy always works for Roman numerals because values are canonical
Use parallel arrays (values[i] maps to symbols[i]) for clean mapping
common_mistakes: Forgetting subtractive forms (CM=900, CD=400, XC=90...) — essential for correctness
Using += for string concatenation instead of string.str_concat
Not subtracting the value after appending the symbol
